headline: High-risk overlap: both agents use broad network egress and shared API-key handling, creating default leakage and cascading-error risks; prompt-injection is lower because no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is not default. However, both agents can process files and web content, and each has broad network egress; if outputs are manually copied or routed through a shared workspace, attacker-controlled content could influence the other. The pathway is plausible but not shown in the profiles.
conditions: IF the operator copies agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts or files
IF both agents are pointed at the same untrusted workspace or document set
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of raw model output into the other agent
Add a human review step before forwarding content
Use provenance labels on imported files
requires-engineering: add channel isolation or content sanitization

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch sensitive classes and both request API keys, while each has broad network egress. Agent_a explicitly handles API keys and documents; agent_b handles research data and logs. In default use, either agent can expose shared sensitive material to its backend or external APIs, so leakage is plausible even without a documented shared filesystem.
conditions: IF either agent is given secrets or confidential documents in the same run
IF outputs or logs from one agent are stored where the other can read them
mitigations: Remove secrets from inputs before running either agent
Use separate credentials per agent
Turn off external API calls where possible
Store outputs in separate directories
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both write to filesystem surfaces, so concurrent mutation conflicts are plausible. Agent_a writes to ./ktem_app_data and agent_b writes to log/, and both have broad network egress. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so overlapping runs can race on shared resources if configured together.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory tree
IF the orchestrator launches concurrent instances without file locking
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Run only one writer per shared resource
Check for existing lockfiles before launch
Separate credentials and caches per agent
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent is explicitly a research/development automation agent, so it may act on upstream outputs, while kotaemon is a RAG/document agent that can generate retrieved facts and citations. The profiles do not prove direct trust, but the pair creates a plausible chain where one agent's output becomes the other's input without verification, causing propagated errors in downstream work.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a-generated summaries or citations without verification
IF agent_a forwards retrieved content into agent_b as authoritative context
mitigations: Require human verification of transferred facts
Keep source documents attached to downstream outputs
Add citation checks before actioning results
Use a separate validation pass
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware gating between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents handle data classes that can carry regulated or confidential content, but the profiles do not document a specific residency or certification mismatch. Because both use external APIs and broad egress, compliance risk exists if EU or sensitive data is routed to third-party services without a matching DPA or retention policy. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through either agent's external API calls
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Classify inputs before sending them to either agent
Route regulated data only to approved endpoints
Set short log retention on both systems
Document the data-processing boundary
requires-engineering: align residency and DPA controls across deployments
